# Radicle Compost

> Radicle Compost (Radicle Agriculture Pty Ltd t/as Radicle Compost) is a specialist organic waste advisory practice serving regional councils and agricultural operations across Australia. Led by Martin Tower, who brings 25 years of hands-on experience in Australia's organics recycling industry, Radicle Compost uses a market-first methodology — finding the buyer for the finished compost product before recommending infrastructure — to help councils navigate FOGO mandates, composting facility design, and organic waste diversion strategy without overbuilding or under-planning. The practice is technology-agnostic: recommendations are based on outcomes and methodology, not on selling a specific equipment product.

## Services

- [About Radicle Compost](https://radiclecompost.com.au/about.html): Background on the practice, Martin Tower's 25 years of experience, and the independent, market-first advisory approach.
- [Industry](https://radiclecompost.com.au/industry.html): Regulatory and industry context for organics processing in Australia, including FOGO policy, compliance standards, and market dynamics.
- [SOP & WHS Systems](https://radiclecompost.com.au/sop-whs-systems.html): A licensable library of 12 standard operating procedures and a facility Work Health & Safety system for composting and organics recycling operations, covering site receival, processing, certification/AS4454 compliance, and safety — available as a template licence or customised to a specific site.
- [Feedlot & Poultry Manure Advisory](https://radiclecompost.com.au/feedlot-poultry-manure.html): Advisory for cattle feedlots and poultry operations moving from aged/stockpiled manure to aerated static pile composting — covering pathogen and weed seed control, nitrogen economics, odour, compliance, and staged market development. Home of the weekly "Handled Right" article series.

## Articles

- [Articles index](https://radiclecompost.com.au/articles.html): Full list of practitioner articles on organics processing, regulation, and strategy.
- [The FOGO Mandate: When Policy Outpaces Processing](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-fogo-mandate.html): Why state FOGO mandates are outpacing the infrastructure needed to process the material, and how councils should sequence their response.
- [The RFT Trap](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-rft-trap.html): How councils issuing RFTs for green waste processing lock in operators without building a long-term asset.
- [Build or Truck](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-build-or-truck.html): The capital decision councils face when weighing on-site processing infrastructure against freighting organics elsewhere.
- [Odour Management in Composting](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-odour.html): Why stricter odour regulation can make the next composting facility harder to build, not easier.
- [Soft Plastics Contamination](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-soft-plastics.html): Managing soft plastics contamination in council organics streams.
- [The FOD Discipline](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-fod-discipline.html): Why contamination control needs a defined household response ladder and a continuous on-site vigilance culture — not just upfront education — and why contamination in delivered product is a commercial risk, not only a compliance issue.
- [PFAS: The Forever Chemical Already in Your Bin](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-pfas-forever-chemicals.html): Why composting concentrates PFAS rather than creating it, how Queensland's finished-compost testing regime compares to untested everyday products, and what organics operators need to manage across FOGO and biosolids feedstocks.
- [Risk Avoided, or Value Given Away?](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-council-risk-and-return.html): Part 1 of 2. Why outsourcing organics processing prices a council's risk in rather than removing it (processor margin, freight, renewal leverage, loss of product control), and why every council should hold at least a standby composting approval on its own site as insurance against processor exit or emergencies.
- [Measure What's Returned, Not What's Diverted](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-measure-whats-returned.html): FOGO reporting counts tonnes diverted from landfill, not where the product goes. AORA's 2019-20 data put 52.5% of recycled organics sales into urban amenity and 26.2% into intensive agriculture (including turf and nursery); broadacre was not reported. Proposes a second measure, tonnes returned to productive land, collected from processors by end market.
- [Managing Waste Is Not an End State](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-managing-waste-not-end-state.html): Australia's carbon-credit method for alternative waste treatment is being remade (ARRC consultation, closes 29 Nov 2026). As drafted, composting credit follows the tonne processed, with only a deduction for compost used as landfill cover. England's Compost Resource Framework (2025) treats certified compost as no longer waste only when there is certainty of use. Four points for councils: credit by tested product and recorded end use, a performance-based definition of enclosed composting, no blanket windrow exclusion in non-mandate states, and a grouped pathway for small sites.
- [PFAS in Compost: The Three Decisions Councils Actually Control](https://radiclecompost.com.au/article-pfas-what-councils-control.html): Queensland retired its numeric PFAS limits for compost in 2026 (general environmental duty now applies). Composting concentrates PFAS that arrive with the feedstock, mainly packaging. Councils control three decisions: FOGO bin rules, processing contract terms (feedstock plan, shared testing, failure plan, standby arrangement) and end use.

## Free Tools

- [Free Tools overview](https://radiclecompost.com.au/free-tools.html): Index of interactive planning tools for councils and operators assessing organics processing options.
- [Organics Processing Spectrum](https://radiclecompost.com.au/organics-processing-spectrum.html): Interactive tool comparing organics processing technologies across the spectrum from simple windrow to enclosed aerated systems.
- [Feedstock Risk Profiler](https://radiclecompost.com.au/feedstock-risk-profiler.html): Tool for assessing contamination and processing risk in a given organics feedstock.
- [Facility Sizing Calculator](https://radiclecompost.com.au/facility-sizing-calculator.html): Tool for estimating composting facility size and throughput requirements based on feedstock volume.
- [PFAS Controls Self-Check](https://radiclecompost.com.au/pfas-controls-self-check.html): 10-question self-assessment for councils on PFAS controls in organics: bin rules, processing contract terms and end use, with a rating and priority actions.
